Enabled by default.name: Enhanced Canvas TextMetrics
Enabled by default.summary:
Expand the Canvas 2D text API to support text shaping inspection, selection rectangles, bounding box queries, and glyph run/cluster rendering.

This new functionality should enable complex text editing applications with accurate selection, caret positioning, and hit testing.  Additionally, cluster-based rendering facilitates sophisticated text effects such as independent character animations and styling.
Enabled by default.creator: fmalita@chromium.org

maturity.text: Specification currently under development in a Working Group

view.notes:
WebKit supports the problem space—enabling canvas text shaping, cluster rendering, and selection—and objected to the earlier `TextMetrics`-based API design on WHATWG issue #10677, subsequently publishing an alternative `CanvasTextShaping` sketch (https://github.com/WebKit/explainers/pull/137).

Prior to shipping, we redesigned this proposal around `shapeText()`, `ShapedText`, `GlyphRun`, and `fillGlyphRun(s)` / `strokeGlyphRun(s)` (leaving `TextMetrics` unchanged) to align with WebKit's core shaping architecture while deferring multi-style `FormattedText` and `Intl.Segmenter` extensions to a future phase.

Strongly Positive

There is strong demand from canvas-heavy frameworks and applications that implement custom text layout and text editing. Canvas text rendering currently suffers from significant performance and memory overhead because applications are forced to synchronize offscreen DOM elements just to measure selection rectangles, bounding boxes, and caret positions.

Key validation from the ~8-month Origin Trial:

* Flutter Web: Integrated and validated the capability in their production engine (WebParagraph) throughout the Origin Trial, and migrated to the updated `shapeText()` / `ShapedText` / `GlyphRun` surface (`glyphClusters()`, `selectionRects()`, `actualBoundingBox()`, `fillGlyphRun()`). They rely on these primitives to drive their web text layout and hit-testing, and are strongly advocating for shipping this capability.

* Canvas Tooling & Creative Coding: Successfully demonstrated in complex single-line typography scenarios, such as interactive text-on-a-path editors and per-glyph animations, without requiring DOM-based synchronization.

Enabled by default.name: Prompt API Sampling Mode
Enabled by default.summary:
Allows developers to configure language model output variety and creativity in the Prompt API using high-level samplingMode presets. Instead of exposing raw numerical parameters like topK and temperature that vary unpredictably across models, developers can choose semantic presets ranging from "most-predictable" for deterministic extraction to "most-creative" for open-ended brainstorming. The browser maps these presets to optimal sampling hyperparameters for the underlying model, providing developers with reliable response tuning while preserving cross-browser interoperability.

enum LanguageModelSamplingMode {
  "most-predictable",      // For strict consistency/factual extraction
  "predictable",           // For highly focused outputs
  "slightly-predictable",  // For moderately focused, consistent outputs
  "balanced",              // The default state for standard prompting
  "slightly-creative",     // For moderately varied, expressive outputs
  "creative",              // For tasks favoring variety over strict facts
  "most-creative"          // For maximum token diversity and brainstorming
};

This feature is an enhancement of the Prompt API (https://chromestatus.com/feature/5134603979063296).
Enabled by default.creator: memmott@google.com

maturity.text: Specification being incubated in a Community Group

view.notes: View reflects parent specification
View reflects parent specification

Relative to the current shipped baseline (no sampling control on the web, since raw temperature and topK were excluded per TAG guidance), a significant fraction of developers support adding samplingMode to steer output variance, though a subset would still prefer the raw knobs:

Developer Demand & Surveys: When asked to compare presets directly against raw parameters, 75% of parameter-tuning Early Preview Program (EPP) respondents accepted presets (55% preferred presets outright, 20% were open to them), while 25% would still prefer raw temperature / topK floats. Interoperable presets also address concerns from EPP sign-ups, where 33% flagged “Cross-Engine Prompt Fragility” (needing per-model tuning) and 22% cited “API Configuration Gaps” (e.g. inability to tune). The number of presets expanded from 5 to 7 options, partly in response to OT developer feedback around gaps in the predictable end of the spectrum.

Telemetry: Across the modest samplingMode OT and the larger legacy (temperature & topK) Chrome extension usage, over 95% of tuned sessions opt for predictable outputs, with 75% choosing most-predictable and >60% setting equivalent parameters (temperature = 0 / topK = 1).

Adoption Examples: Origin Trial partners (production e-commerce platforms, merchant website builders, and shopping extensions) and open-source projects rely on most-predictable and predictable (often paired with responseConstraint) for deterministic tasks such as catalog attribute extraction, merchant copywriting tools, intent classification, analysis of administrative procedures survey data by a governmental agency, and extraction of audio impairments from clinical report images.

Other signals: The API implementation can deliver mode-specific inference speedups like Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) speculative decoding in most-predictable sessions (75% of parameter overrides, per our telemetry). This benefits users and developers by providing quicker responses while consuming less compute and power resources.

Edge: Positive (https://github.com/webmachinelearning/prompt-api/issues/203) Microsoft confirmed the API shape is interoperable, even if backends offer less granularity. They would have liked stronger signals regarding granularity, especially on the creative side.

Enabled by default.name: SVG Path Data API
Enabled by default.summary:
Adds structured JavaScript access to SVG path data through three methods on SVGPathElement: getPathData() reads the path as an array of {type, values} objects containing each segment's command and numeric parameters. setPathData() updates the path from such an array, getPathSegmentAtLength() returns the segment at a specified distance along the path. The optional getPathData({normalize: true}) setting simplifies path data to absolute move, line, cubic Bézier, and close commands (M, L, C, and Z). All three APIs operate on the base value of the d attribute, not CSS-computed or animated values.

Enabled by default.name: Spec-compliant XML MIME type detection
Enabled by default.summary:
To fully align with Web standards, Chrome is updating how it detects [XML MIME](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc7303/) types. Chrome will now recognize valid MIME types whose subtype ends in `+xml` as XML across Chrome and Android WebView, including non-application types such as `text/example+xml` and `image/example+xml`.

For these responses, `PerformanceResourceTiming.contentType` returns application/xml. The value for image/svg+xml remains unchanged.

Enterprise web applications that rely on previous `contentType` values may observe behavior changes. Chrome Actor also uses this shared XML classification for dangerous MIME type navigation checks, so it may block navigations to additional non-application +xml responses. Admins should check whether their applications depend on these MIME types or the previous `contentType` values.
Enabled by default.creator: choiwonik91@gmail.com

maturity.text: Final published standard: Recommendation, Living Standard, Candidate Recommendation, or similar final form

view.notes:
Mozilla has an existing positive position on content-type in Resource Timing. I asked whether that position also covers this XML MIME minimization change; confirmation is pending.

In the local Firefox 157.0.1 tests on October 9, 2026, XHR parsed the tested non-application +xml responses as XML. However, PerformanceResourceTiming.contentType retained text/example+xml, image/example+xml and font/example+xml rather than minimizing them to application/xml.

WebKit confirmed that this change is covered by its existing support for content-type in Resource Timing, since MIME minimization was a condition of that support.

This is a standards position, not a statement of implementation status. In the local Safari 26.5 tests on October 9, 2026, PerformanceResourceTiming.contentType was undefined.

Enabled by default.name: WebAppLaunch: user activation on focus-existing launch delivery
Enabled by default.summary: Grants transient user activation to an installed web app's existing window when a launch is delivered into it through the launch_handler "focus-existing" client mode. Origin trial.name: Opening links in a split tab
Origin trial.summary:
Split screen scenarios are increasingly common. In addition to dual screen devices (i.e. physical split screen), many browsers have a split tab (i.e. virtual split screen) feature, where two tabs are tiled side-by-side within a single browser window. When using a split tab, there are multiple cases in which users want to open a link and view it side-by-side with the source page.

Today there is no way for a web author to request that a navigation open into a split tab. The existing navigation targets (_blank, _self, _parent, _top) cannot express this, and windowFeatures only offers popup, which opens a separate, detached browser window. Without popup, window.open() opens the content as a new full-size tab in the current window, which is the only other option available.

This feature provides methods (imperative and declarative) for web authors to request that a link open in a split tab, alongside the current page.
Origin trial.creator: masonfreed@google.com

maturity.text: Proposal in a personal repository, no adoption from community

view.notes: Private feedback is quite positive.
